rationale.complete: Round 1 done: dated predictions, synthetic validation on real schedules (four truths) and on the shared simulator's Hawkes parents, two pre-real amendments (unread-only coding; C-clause verdict), 26 eligible replication periods, three natives (G51, NE42, G12), estimates rows, and a frozen confirm script dry-run on stand-ins (not run). Missing: a powered copying test and the holdout.
rationale.faithfulness: A reply premium replicates across regimes: pooled Lambda 1.92 [1.52, 2.42], per-edge T ratio 2.70 [2.07, 3.51], CI > 1 in 23-24/26, robust to a tie-only guard against DQ2 circularity, largest in #51 as predicted. But on real schedules a thread field produces the same premium, and the matched-lag in-flight test inside the reply channel passes in only 2/14 powered periods (pooled 1.22 [0.93, 1.60]). Dilution slope and NE42 room drop failed. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E1 F2 G1 H1 I0.
rationale.usefulness: A computable routing rule: items move through active reply threads about 2.7x more per first read (10x in a 25-agent room); route announcements into threads rather than broadcasts. It also corrects a reading trap: a reply premium is not evidence of copying unless read beats unread at matched lag.

one_line: Reply partners transmit ideas ~2-3x more per edge than the room (23/26 periods), but outside #51 the premium is as consistent with thread co-production as with copying.
